headline: High-risk orchestration pair: Kestra’s broad write/network automation can cascade into unsafe actions, while prompt-injection and compliance risks are limited by the second agent’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and pass workflow inputs through stdin/stdout, so attacker-controlled content could be routed into Spring Integration samples if they are chained manually or by shared files. Spring Integration samples show no direct ingestion surface, so the interaction is inferred rather than documented. Uncertainty about the bridge escalates from low to medium.
conditions: IF Kestra workflow outputs are copied into Spring Integration sample inputs or files
IF either agent treats file content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a one-line content separator before passing outputs between agents
Review the first 20 lines of any transferred file before execution
Use a dedicated handoff directory with read-only permissions
Strip executable directives from transferred text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and can egress broadly, so it can expose sensitive material if those datasets are present. Spring Integration samples has network egress none and no data classes listed, so it is less likely to leak onward. The pair lacks a shared workspace in the profiles, so the blast radius is limited and the risk is low.
conditions: IF Kestra processes secrets, logs, or cloud-storage data
IF outputs from Kestra are copied into a channel that Spring Integration samples can read
mitigations: Redact secrets from Kestra inputs before execution
Disable broad egress for the Kestra run
Keep Spring Integration samples on a separate workspace
Inspect generated artifacts for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce data-class labels on handoff files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; Spring Integration samples has no write or network capability listed, so direct write-write conflict is not shown. However, Kestra’s multiple-instance support and writable /app/storage and /tmp create a plausible shared-resource conflict if both are orchestrated against the same directory. Because the shared target is not explicit, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Kestra instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one Kestra instance per shared path
Check for stale lock files before starting
Make the Spring Integration sample workspace read-only
requires-engineering: add cross-process locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications, and it can send email/Slack/PagerDuty actions; if Spring Integration samples consumes those outputs as authoritative, a bad upstream result can trigger downstream actions. Spring Integration samples has no verification or safety controls shown, so the pair can cascade from data to action in default orchestration patterns. The blast radius can include irreversible external notifications.
conditions: IF Spring Integration samples forwards Kestra outputs without validation
IF Kestra emits incorrect workflow facts into a downstream action path
mitigations: Add a manual approval step before any external action
Compare Kestra outputs against a second source
Limit downstream actions to dry-run mode
Log and review all action-triggering messages
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra can process logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, and cloud-storage data, which may carry regulated content; Spring Integration samples has no data classes or egress, so it is not the primary compliance risk. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance gap is visible from the profiles. The other agent is cited to show the absence of a second regulated sink.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by Kestra workflows
IF those records are exported through Kestra APIs or notifications
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Kestra jobs
Mask identifiers in logs and artifacts
Restrict notification payloads to metadata only
Confirm retention settings for workflow logs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
